set.hook: A cave à manger on the Faubourg Madeleine: shelves of bottles, one long shared table, a farm-sourced kitchen.
set.why: The room is a wine shop first: bottles line the walls and diners sit at a long communal table, choosing from the shelves. Le Fooding calls it a cave à manger with a long list and a seasonal menu. In the kitchen Martial Blanchon buys from local growers and farmers, and MICHELIN's example plate is warm potatoes with haddock and a tarragon sabayon: plain things, cooked with punch, to set against a serious bottle.
set.verdict: Gault&Millau 2026 gives it 12/20 and lists a six-course menu at 69 euros built from the carte; MICHELIN keeps it in the selection at €€ with no star or Bib. It is the most solid of the Madeleine wine rooms for a guest who wants the bottle and the plate to carry equal weight. Hours differ by source, so call before promising a day.

set.hook: Pépita Del Rosario's natural-wine épicerie and bistrot on the Faubourg Madeleine, trading since 1996.
set.why: Pépita Del Rosario and Richard Grocat opened the Comptoir in 1996 as an épicerie and cave à manger, seeking out small farmers and winemakers who refuse chemical shortcuts, years before natural wine had a following in Beaune. During lockdown the shop side grew into a fuller épicerie and wine shop. The plates are built from what sits on the shelves and from seasonal, organic-leaning produce; reviewers keep returning to the take-away wine list.
set.verdict: A Raisin visitor in mid-2026 praises the list and Pépita herself, so the house trades; whether the table service runs as it once did is less clear, since Raisin and Le Fooding now file it as a shop and TripAdvisor flags it closed. Treat it as a natural-wine cellar first, call to ask about a table, and expect conviction over polish: some reviewers find the service rough.

set.hook: Natural-wine shop and bar off Place Carnot; an open kitchen does bao and shared plates late in the week.
set.why: Enstase opened as a company in September 2021 and works as three things at once: a cellar of natural, organic and biodynamic bottles (some 900 references from small estates, by its own listing), a bar, and a kitchen. Raisin's 2023 feature describes a cooking station that opens two evenings a week for shared plates and street-food bao. Beyond the wine there are ciders, kefirs, kombuchas and juices, which makes it the one counter in town for a guest off alcohol.
set.verdict: The most recent dated evidence is a set of Raisin visitor comments from October 2025; nothing dated 2026 turned up, and listings disagree on which evenings the kitchen runs. It is still the natural-wine counter of central Beaune on paper. Send nobody without a call or a look at its own channels the same week.

set.hook: Beaune's Saturday morning market, under the covered halles and out across Place Fleury.
set.why: On Saturday morning the stalls fill the covered halles on Place de la Halle and spill across Place Fleury: hill-village producers with Époisses and Cîteaux, slabs of jambon persillé, honey, flowers, and in autumn the first wild mushrooms. The same halles host the Hospices wine auction each November, so the market stands where Burgundy sells its most famous barrels. Wednesday brings a smaller food-only market to the same square.
set.verdict: The Office de Tourisme lists it every Saturday from 1 August to 26 December 2026, 08:00-12:00, which is shorter than the 07:00-13:00 our old record gave. Come early for the producers. On auction weekend the halles are the sale room, and no source says whether Saturday 14 November runs as normal, so check with the tourist office before sending guests.

set.hook: Eddy Raillard's charcuterie at 4 rue Monge: jambon persillé, pâté en croûte and boudin blanc over the counter.
set.why: Eddy Raillard, a charcutier from Le Creusot who trained at Bize in Savigny-lès-Beaune, fills his counter on rue Monge with the Burgundian repertoire: jambon persillé set in its green parsley jelly, pâté en croûte, terrine de campagne, boudin blanc, rosette and dry saucisson, and snails in parsley butter. A queue forms on busy mornings. Buy a thick slice and bread nearby and lunch is done standing up.
set.verdict: The shop exists at 4 rue Monge in public listings and a 2025 review, and Pudlowski called the jambon persillé a model of the genre in 2018, but nothing dated 2026 turned up and the hours on record are from 2018. Reviews praise the pâté en croûte and the persillé and grumble about the welcome. Call before you plan a lunch on it.

set.caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday morning in 2018; two phone numbers in circulation; reviews mention a brusque welcome and a queue

set.hook: A former Park Hyatt pastry chef's shop on rue Monge: cheesecake, Saint-Honoré, chocolates, a small tea room.
set.why: Fabien Berteau was Gault&Millau's pastry chef of the year in 2015, working beside Jean-François Rouquette at the Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme, where his cheesecakes were the signature. He then opened his own shop on rue Monge, a short walk from the Hospices. The counter runs from entremets and red-fruit tarts to bonbons de chocolat, and the cheesecake came with him; a small salon de thé lets you eat the cake on the spot.
set.verdict: Gault&Millau keeps him in its artisan listing and directory pages were updated in February 2026, but no review or post dated 2026 surfaced, so trading is likely rather than proven. The pastry is the reason to go; several reviewers find the service cool. The Sunday-morning opening makes it one of the few good stops on auction Sunday.

wine.title: Bottles first, plates second
wine.story: East of the walls, the Faubourg Madeleine is where Beaune drinks off the négoce circuit. Le Comptoir des Tontons opened there in 1996, when Pépita Del Rosario and Richard Grocat began stocking growers who refused chemical shortcuts; today it trades mainly as an épicerie and natural-wine cellar. A few doors down, Caves Madeleine seats diners at a shared table among its shelves, and Gault&Millau 2026 rates Martial Blanchon's farm-sourced cooking 12/20. Back inside the ramparts, Enstase stocks about 900 natural, organic and biodynamic references and opens a bao kitchen on chosen evenings. In all three the bottle comes off a shelf you can touch, and the food is cooked to suit it.
wine.where: Caves Madeleine, Faubourg Madeleine; Le Comptoir des Tontons, Faubourg Madeleine; Enstase, Place Carnot

street.title: Market, charcutier, pâtissier
street.story: Beaune's street food is bought at a counter and eaten standing up. On Saturday mornings, 08:00 to 12:00 by the tourist office's 2026 listing, the market fills the covered halles and Place Fleury with Époisses, Cîteaux and jambon persillé, in the same halles where the Hospices sell their wine each November. Two streets away on rue Monge, Eddy Raillard's charcuterie at number 4 sells the persillé Gilles Pudlowski called a model of the genre in 2018, alongside pâté en croûte and boudin blanc. At number 18, Fabien Berteau, Gault&Millau's pastry chef of the year in 2015, sells the cheesecake he made his name with at the Park Hyatt in Paris.
street.where: Marché des Halles, Place de la Halle; Charcuterie Raillard, Place Monge; Pâtisserie Fabien Berteau, Rue Monge
